name: The Sudd (Ramsar wetland)
blurb: A vast White Nile swamp where floods feed grasses, fish, birds and antelope.

tip.title: Shrink the flood
tip.text: The White Nile flood spreads over the plain each year. Lower White Nile flood pulse by 50% and watch the floodplain grasses, then lechwe, kob, hippos and crocodiles.

notes: The species list comes from GBIF occurrence records inside a circle around the park, so it can include nearby areas. Feeding links come from GloBI records and the sources listed where they state them; others are general ecology and are illustrative.

nodes.desc: Strong tropical light drives rapid growth of floodplain grasses, papyrus and algae in the shallow water.
Floodplain grasses stand tall in the rains and are often burned in the dry season, renewing grazing for wildlife and livestock.

nodes.name: Decomposers
nodes.desc: Bacteria and fungi break down dead swamp vegetation and carcasses, returning nutrients to the water and soil.
A tall sedge forming dense stands and floating mats in the Sudd, shaping habitat for birds such as the shoebill.
Microscopic algae in the open water and channels, grazed by fish and small animals.

nodes.name: White-eared kob
nodes.desc: A grazing antelope whose huge seasonal herds migrate across the grasslands of South Sudan.
Spends the day in water and grazes grasses on land at night; it lives in the Sudd shallows.
A common fish of the Sudd that feeds largely on algae and plant material, and is prey for many larger animals.
A large fish-eating waterbird that uses the Sudd and its channels.
A fish-eating eagle of African lakes and rivers that takes fish from the surface of open water.
A small scavenging vulture recorded near the Sudd that feeds on carcasses and scraps.
A top predator of the swamp that eats fish and ambushes antelope at the water edge.
A top predator of South Sudan savannas that hunts grazing antelope such as kob and tiang.
